# Recreation Prompt

Recreate `Afterglow Static`, a mobile-first portrait visual novel based on this prompt: Euphoria neon teen-drama narrative. An Euphoria neon teen-drama narrative game with hyper-stylized nightlife, emotional chaos, identity crisis, romance toxicity, vulnerability, digital-age intimacy, and glittery melancholy with mobile-first controls, touch-friendly interactions, responsive readability, optimized on game start for portrait UI format, and the best-adapted mobile UX version targeting portrait aspect ratios in the 4:7 to 9:16 range.

Preserve the source mechanics exactly: one start CTA, tap/click dialogue advancement, typewriter skip, one two-choice branch, two route endings, and restart. Build as a single browser-native HTML file with inline CSS/JS and canvas ambience.

World identity: Nova, a phone-lit teen at a neon afterparty, must choose between a toxic DM spiral and vulnerable honesty with Jules. Visual language should include magenta/cyan/violet glass UI, cracked mirrors, message shards, club strobe, rooftop skyline, glitter particles, and phone glow. Keep all controls large and readable in 4:7 to 9:16 portrait.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source truth
The preserved source is a single-file browser visual novel: start overlay, animated canvas background, dialogue panel with typewriter text, tap/click advance, tap-to-skip typing, one two-button choice, two route endings, audio/GIF feedback, and restart. There are no collision, physics, score, timer, inventory, or movement mechanics.

## Protected mechanics
- Start button enters active story state.
- Dialogue panel advances one line at a time and skips typewriter text when tapped mid-line.
- A single decision point presents exactly two choices.
- Choice buttons route to one of two terminal branches.
- End overlay stops active story animation/audio and exposes restart.
- Restart returns to the first scene and repeats the same state graph.

## Remixed target
`Afterglow Static` preserves that visual-novel structure while reinterpreting the story as a neon teen-drama night about Nova, a phone-lit student navigating identity performance, toxic romance, vulnerability, and digital-age intimacy.

## Mechanic decomposition
- Input: protected; click/tap buttons and dialogue panel.
- Timing: protected; requestAnimationFrame ambience plus typewriter interval.
- Branching: protected; opening scene -> meeting scene -> two choices -> two endings.
- HUD: themable; scene chip, speaker label, dialogue, CTA copy.
- Visuals: safe to transform; beach boardwalk becomes neon hallway/mirror/club/rooftop.
- Media: safe accents only; catalog-backed audio and GIFs.

## Safe theming surfaces
Canvas scene ownership, character silhouette, route language, title, HUD vocabulary, font, palette, ambient glitter, phone/D.M. motifs, feedback GIF moments, and route-complete labels.
